blocks.x: The Achala IT Solutions build of Real-Time Streaming & Event-Driven Decisioning: concrete interfaces at core systems, measured movement on event-to-action latency, and a delivery rhythm your control owners can plan around from week one.
Real-Time Streaming & Event-Driven Decisioning exists because the hard part of this work is not the model — it is the measurement, the ownership and the audit trail. That is what this page describes.

blocks.title: Governed lakehouse pipeline — Real-Time Streaming & Event-Driven Decisioning
blocks.note: Each stage passes its output forward under a typed contract — schema, owner and freshness agreed in advance; the audit path shares the timeline with the data path.

blocks.x: Real-Time Streaming & Event-Driven Decisioning runs on a structure your control owners can interrogate — the decision plane, the evidence plane and the governance plane stay separate in design and reconciled in operation.

The build sequence is deliberate: contracts and identity first, the working decision slice second, the verification harness third — because a Real-Time Streaming & Event-Driven Decisioning capability without its eval gate is just another unattended automation.

blocks.title: Delivery cadence — Real-Time Streaming & Event-Driven Decisioning
blocks.note: The cadence is the governance: baseline at the start, evidence generated as work happens, gates with stop authority on fixed dates.

items: Metric anarchy
One definition per metric, owned and versioned — the dashboard and the board pack cannot disagree.
Cost creep
Unit costs on a published budget with alerts at the threshold — creep is caught by the meter, not by the invoice.
Silent schema drift
Contracts enforced at the boundary — schema drift fails the pipeline loudly, in minutes.
